key_insight: The paper shows how to generate graphs that match a target persistence diagram exactly, rather than only approximately, by using either iterative local rules or a complete global constraint-satisfaction formulation.
engineering_relevance: This enables topology-controlled graph generation for computational science workflows where exact structural guarantees matter, such as design, synthesis, and benchmarking.
method: Local method: iteratively construct degree-based PD-equivalent graphs and prove every output matches the target PD.
Local method: show reachability of all degree-based PD-equivalent graphs, but note a trade-off with diversity and infeasible states.

Global method: encode exact topological compliance as a complete constraint program solvable by modern solvers; works for vertex-based permutation-equivariant filtrations and is minimal under degree filtration.
evidence_signal: Experiments on four standard graph-generation benchmarks show that both methods realize the target persistence diagram exactly.
watch_item: The local approach can reduce sample diversity and may encounter infeasible states, while the global solver-based approach may depend on constraint-programming scalability.
paper_title: Exact Topological Compliance: Generating Persistence-Equivalent Graphs
